stem: A local dispatch has capacity 10 kg; packets cannot split. A weighs 6 kg, due today, priority 2; B weighs 4 kg, due today, priority 1; C weighs 3 kg, due tomorrow, priority 1; D weighs 4 kg, due today, priority 2. First maximize the NUMBER due today, then among ties minimize the SUM of their priority numbers, then choose greatest total weight. Tomorrow packets may fill leftover capacity. Which load is chosen?
explanation: At most two today packets fit: A+B 10 kg, A+D 10 kg, B+D 8 kg. Priority sums 3,4,3 eliminate A+D; greatest weight selects A+B. B+C+D exceeds 10 kg. Counting priorities before the number of due packets misapplies the lexicographic rule.
